item.text: {"text":"Closest direct precedent: [HSTU-BLaIR (2025)](https://kdd2025llm4ecommerce.github.io/assets/accepted/13_HSTU_BLaIR_Lightweight_Cont.pdf) augments HSTU item representations with contrastive text embeddings and reports improvements over ID-only HSTU across Amazon and Steam experiments. However, its BLaIR encoder uses pretraining on reviews and metadata; these results do not establish that a title/description encoder trained from scratch will help under the supplied constraints. [ST2SI (COLING 2025)](https://aclanthology.org/2025.coling-main.171/) separately motivates aligning textual representations with item IDs: semantic representations alone can miss behavioral transition patterns. Neither establishes reliable product compatibility inference from lexical similarity.\n\nA constraint-compatible hypothesis, rather than a published finding: retain HSTU and jointly train a small token/subword title-description encoder, fuse its projection with ID embeddings, and optimize next-item prediction with a modest auxiliary ID–text alignment loss. Use the same fused item representation for history inputs and candidate scoring, keeping all parameters in one checkpoint per category. Compare separate experimental conditions—ID-only, text fusion, and text fusion with lexical hard negatives—using the fixed macro validation HR@10; never combine their predictions. Lexically similar negatives could test discrimination beyond broad topic overlap, but may include valid alternatives and require cautious weighting. Missing model numbers, connector specifications, or explicit compatibility statements should remain unknown; observed interaction transitions provide behavioral evidence, not verified compatibility labels."}
